extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form paragraphs for examining patent applications under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103 and for assessing specification requirements under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description, enablement, best mode), including special rules for computer-implemented inventions and transitional/priority issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.103
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the statute is being applied, but is not cited in an action on the merits, use paragraph 7.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should only be used ONCE in a given Office action. When this form paragraph is used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections, it must precede specified AIA form paragraphs (7.20.01.aia, 7.20.02.aia, 7.20.04.aia, 7.20.05.aia, 7.21.aia, 7.21.01.aia, 7.21.02.aia, and 7.22.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.20.01.aia — 103 Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) Because Reference is Prior Art Under 102(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when applicant has submitted that the claimed invention and subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference were commonly owned or subject to obligation of assignment or developed under a joint research agreement, yet the subject matter is excepted under 102(a)(2) but still qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome the rejection under 102(a)(1) by a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the subject matter was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor and thus not prior art under 102(b)(1)(A), or rely on exception under 102(b)(1)(B) by providing evidence of a prior public disclosure. Examiner notes: use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (AIA) and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia; include after 7.20.aia or 7.15.aia when 103 rejection is based on subject matter excepted under 102(b)(2)(C). In brackets identify common assignee and the reference that has been excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.20.02.aia — Joint Inventors, Common Ownership Presumed
rubrics_metrics.description: When application names joint inventors, the examiner presumes subject matter of various claims was commonly owned at the time inventions were effectively filed absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and effective filing dates of each claim not commonly owned so examiner can consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). Examiner notes: use only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013; must be preceded by 7.03.aia; use in all applications with joint inventors unless claims clearly restricted to only one claimed invention (e.g., single claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.20.04.aia — 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Prior Art Attempted to be Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) (Common Ownership/Assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when applicant attempted to show subject matter in a reference is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) by showing common ownership or assignment but failed to provide the required conspicuous statement; therefore the subject matter is not excepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file the required submission to properly except the subject matter (see MPEP § 2154.02(c)). Alternatives include showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained from the inventor or providing evidence of prior public disclosure under 37 CFR 1.130(b) (102(b)(2)(B)). Examiner notes: use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia; include when 103 rejection is based on a reference excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) but no proper statement was provided; bracket guidance: identify applied art and common assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.20.05.aia — 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Prior Art Attempted to be Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) (Joint Research Agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when applicant attempted to show exception under 102(b)(2)(C) by relying on joint research agreement provisions of 35 U.S.C. 102(c) but failed to provide required materials/statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file missing requirements to properly except the subject matter (see 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) and 1.104(c)(4)(ii)). Alternatives: show under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained from the inventor, or provide evidence under 37 CFR 1.130(b). Examiner notes: include in all actions containing obviousness or anticipation rejections where an attempt to except subject matter via joint research agreement is ineffective; bracket guidance: identify the reference and the reason(s) attempt is ineffective (e.g., failure to submit required statement or amend specification to include names of parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.21.aia — Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 (Obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph applies to AIA applications (filed on/after March 16, 2013) and must be preceded by 7.03.aia and by either form paragraph 7.20.aia or 7.103. An explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144). If rejection is provisional based on a copending application that would be prior art under 102(a)(2) if published/patented, use 7.21.01.aia instead. Bracket guidance: insert claim numbers and prior art relied upon; for applications claiming priority to pre-March 16, 2013 filing, must be preceded by 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.21.01.aia — Provisional 103 Rejection Over Copending Application (Common Assignee/Applicant/Inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 as obvious over a copending application that has a common assignee/applicant or at least one common (joint) inventor; based on presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application which would qualify as prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be overcome by: (1) 37 CFR 1.130(a) showing subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) 37 CFR 1.130(b) showing prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (3) a statement under 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement. Examiner notes: use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia; used to provisionally reject claims over a copending application that discloses the claimed invention and would constitute prior art under 102(a)(2) if published or patented; bracket guidance for inserting claim numbers, application number, and whether common assignee/applicant/joint inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.22.aia — 103 Rejection 'Further in View Of'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2] as applied to claim [3] above, and further in view of [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket guidance: insert assignee/applicant/joint inventor where required. An explanation of the obviousness rejection must be included (see MPEP § 2144). If claimed invention is not patentably distinct from the invention claimed in a copending application, a provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection should also be made using form paragraphs 8.33 and 8.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.21.02.aia — 103 Rejection, Common Assignee/Applicant/Inventor (AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over [2], where the applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application and on its effectively earlier filing date constitutes prior art under 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection may be overcome by: (1) 37 CFR 1.130(a) showing subject matter was obtained from inventor/joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)); (2) 37 CFR 1.130(b) prior public disclosure (102(b)(2)(B)); or (3) a statement under 102(b)(2)(C). Examiner notes: use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013; must be preceded by 7.21.aia; an explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.23.aia — Test for Obviousness (Graham factors summarized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual inquiries for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103: (1) determining the scope and contents of the prior art; (2) ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue; (3) resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art; (4) considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph when appropriate in response to arguments regarding applicability of the factors for determining obviousness. Examiner notes: use only in AIA applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.27.aia — Rejection Under 102 or 103 (Anticipation or Obviousness Alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102([2]) as anticipated by or, in the alternative, under 35 U.S.C. 103 as obvious over [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is NOT intended as a common substitute for a single rejection under 102 or 103; a single rejection should be made whenever possible. Examples of appropriate circumstances include: (a) disputed claim interpretation where one interpretation yields 102 and another yields 103 (see MPEP §§ 2111-2116.01); (b) reference discloses all limitations except a property or function and examiner cannot determine inherent possession vs obvious variant (In re Fitzgerald); (c) genus/species issues (In re Schaumann); (d) product-by-process issues where product appears the same though produced by different process (In re Marosi, In re Thorpe); (e) means-plus-function uncertainty (MPEP §§ 2183-2184); (f) overlapping ranges where reference lacks specific example in claimed range (Ex parte Lee). Examiner notes: if claims are indefinite, a 112(b) rejection may be appropriate; a full explanation must follow; must be preceded by 7.07.aia and related paragraphs and for priority matters by 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2159.01 — Applications Filed Before March 16, 2013 (Pre-AIA Governing Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 in the AIA do not apply to any application filed before March 16, 2013; such applications are governed by pre‑AIA 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE or entering the national stage does not constitute filing a new application; adding claims after March 16, 2013 that contain new matter does not make AIA apply because 35 U.S.C. 132(a) prohibits new matter. Amendments believed to contain new matter: (1) new drawings should not be entered if they contain new matter; (2) amendments to written description/claims with new matter are ordinarily entered but new matter must be canceled and claims directed to new matter rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (see MPEP §§ 608.02, 608.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2159.02 — Applications Filed On or After March 16, 2013 (When AIA Applies)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 apply to any patent application that contains or contained at any time a claim to a claimed invention having an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013. If there is ever even a single such claim, AIA 102/103 apply to the application and to the patentability of every claimed invention in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application filed on/after March 16, 2013 is amended to contain a claim with an effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013 (i.e., becomes an AIA application), the amendment must have support under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) in the application filed on/after March 16, 2013. The application becomes subject to AIA even if the newly added claim is subsequently canceled. If an amendment causes a change from pre-AIA to AIA applicability, any new ground of rejection necessitated by the change is considered a new ground of rejection necessitated by an amendment for purposes of finality (see MPEP § 706.07(a)). Applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 that, as originally filed, disclose and claim only subject matter in an earlier pre‑March 16 application to which it is entitled to priority are treated as pre-AIA applications for this purpose; adding claims to new matter does not change this unless the new claim has proper support.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2159.03 — Applications Subject to AIA but Also Containing Pre‑March 16, 2013 Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application subject to AIA also contains (or contained at any time) a claim having an effective filing date before March 16, 2013, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) applies to every claim in the application (and to resulting patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, such claims must be patentable under both AIA 102/103 and pre‑AIA 102(g). Care must be taken when subject matter claims priority/benefit to pre‑March 16 applications to determine whether AIA or pre‑AIA 102/103 applies. See MPEP § 2151 for more guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2159.04 — Applicant Statement in Transition Applications (37 CFR 1.55/1.78 Statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional application filed on or after March 16, 2013 (a 'transition application') claims the benefit of or priority to an application with a filing date prior to March 16, 2013 and also contains or contained at any time a claimed invention having an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect (a 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists the Office in determining whether the transition application is subject to AIA 102/103 or pre‑AIA 102/103. Applicant is not required to provide the statement if the transition application claims the benefit of an earlier transition application in which the statement has already been filed (see 37 CFR 1.78(c)(6)(i); see also MPEP § 210).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2161 — Three Separate Specification Requirements under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (or Pre‑AIA 112, First Paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include (A) a written description of the invention; (B) the manner and process of making and using the invention (enablement); and (C) the best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) language: specification shall contain a written description and of the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the same, and shall set forth the best mode contemplated. These three requirements are separate and distinct; written description is not interchangeable with enablement. Case citations: Ariad (en banc), Vas‑Cath, In re Barker, Vasudevan Software v. MicroStrategy, and others explaining separateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy the written description requirement, the specification must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail that one skilled in the art can reasonably conclude the inventor had possession of the claimed invention at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is to ensure the scope of the claims does not overreach the inventor's contribution. Disclosure may be adequate without speaking in haec verba of claim language; adequacy depends on state of the art and nature/breadth of the claimed genus/species. Case citations: Reiffin, LizardTech, Hynix v. Rambus, Rivera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must disclose the manner and process of making and using the invention 'in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms' as to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement is distinct from written description: an invention may be described without being enabled (e.g., a compound without a method of making), and a disclosure may enable without describing particular claimed subject matter. See In re Armbruster for distinction examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must 'set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor or joint inventor of carrying out the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best mode is a separate requirement; case law (In re Newton) recognizes distinctness from enablement and written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2161.01 — Computer‑implemented inventions: written description and functional claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer‑implemented inventions, statutory requirements (subject matter eligibility, utility, novelty, nonobviousness, definiteness, and the three 112(a) requirements) apply as with all inventions. Claims with computer‑implemented functional limitations may invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (means‑plus‑function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a claim is not construed as means‑plus‑function under 112(f), computer‑implemented functional claim language must be evaluated for sufficient disclosure under written description and enablement. To satisfy written description for a functional limitation, the specification must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail to show possession at filing. There is no special rule for supporting a genus by species disclosure; whether a genus is supported depends on the art and the nature/breadth of the genus. Case citations: Ariad, Reiffin, LizardTech, Hynix, Rivera; examples and guidance on genus/species support and breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation standards for functional/means‑plus‑function limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional claim limitations (including those potentially invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f)) must be assessed for adequate written description and enablement; if construed under 112(f), structure corresponding to the function must be sufficiently disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the specification conveys to one skilled in the art that the inventor possessed the claimed functional invention at filing and provides sufficient structure/algorithm (for computer implementations) to support the claim scope. See MPEP § 2181 for means‑plus‑function guidance and related subsections on algorithms and structures.
